decisions.reason: As a standard rye country bread in the bakery’s core everyday segment, it is likely to stay because it fits habitual household demand despite some overlap with other dark breads.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen remains very likely to stay because it is a highlighted flagship seasonal product backed by an award and supports both prestige and holiday sales.
The rye mixed bread with seeds should remain because it combines the firm’s traditional bread strengths with broad customer appeal for hearty seeded loaves.
This dark barley malt rye bread is the most exposed to rationalisation because it is more niche and overlaps with other rye products, but it still suits the artisanal bakery profile.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is likely to remain as a classic holiday variant that complements the stronger flagship stollen and supports seasonal gift demand.
The ancient grain bread is likely to stay because its natural, traditional grain mix fits the firm’s craft-based positioning and gives some differentiation within the bread assortment.
